blockers.quote: Your phone is up, thumb refreshing: the bus app, the result page, mother's typing dots. The chai glass slips off the counter and smashes on the floor. You look down. It is still in your hand.
blockers.why: story #3: the first 10 s show a picture but say nothing. The first spoken line is the title question somewhere before 0:20, so for ten seconds I get no premise and no stakes. The result due Friday is only a page on a phone I can't read at feed size. I see a glass break and not break, but I don't know what I could lose.
blockers.fix: Put the first word within 1 s, spoken over the refresh and the smash: "Result's due Friday. So you check everything before it happens. Tonight, something checks first." Then, as you look down: "Your chai just broke. It's still in your hand." Keep the title question and "You have one minute..." at 0:10 to 0:20.

blockers.quote: College nets: you call the ball before the bowler's arm comes over, swing where the ghost ball goes, and still miss, because the bowler saw you shift.
blockers.why: The viewer's week: batting at the college nets is not in Riya's week (chai, bus or metro, exams, office, family). I would picture someone else's life here, not mine.
blockers.fix: Move the gag to the college canteen TV with friends: "You call the six before the bowler runs in. Your friends stop watching with you." The cricket fact then lands on the batter on screen: the ball beats the eye, so he reads the bowler's body, and you read the minute and it spoils the match instead.

suggestions.quote: A firm spent about three hundred million dollars on a straighter cable to gain about three thousandths of a second
suggestions.fix: This is where I'd leave. The cable, the quake warning and Lorenz come back to back on one train ride where nothing happens to me: three facts in forty seconds is a lecture. Cut the cable beat and keep the quake brake, which I feel under my feet. Let Lorenz land only after grandfather says or does something on that train.

suggestions.quote: Can I just catch the glass, or does it always come true? Answered at 0:40: you catch it, and the ghost redraws.
suggestions.fix: The ghost is a minute ahead, so the real glass should slip at about 1:05, not 0:40. If I count, I stop trusting the rule. Move the catch to the end of the full minute, after the rule beat, and let a ghost-bus line fill the gap.

suggestions.quote: Final year, the result due Friday, and you check everything before it happens: the bus app, the result page, the typing dots.
suggestions.fix: The result is the stake in the opening and never comes back, so I'll wonder about it at the end. Pay it off in the last image: "The result page and mother's dots both glow through the fabric, and you let them."

keep.quote: Being caught out was the gift.
"You've heard it." He does not finish.
